definitions.meaning: first meaning: of the finest quality
second meaning: the act of picking or the thing picked

explanation.surface: A shop or menu boasts of its exquisite range of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means of top quality; as a noun it is an option picked from several.

clue.text: Used chance to embroil one in deception

indicators.note: to embroil is to draw someone into the middle of a situation, so one thing is placed inside another
something used is worn or knocked about, so the letters are treated roughly and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone took a gamble to drag another person into a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicane is trickery or sharp practice, a less common synonym of chicanery used to mean underhand deceit.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put things in sequence
second meaning: a decoration or knighthood conferred by the state

explanation.surface: Someone sets about securing a medal or title for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To put into sequence is one sense; an order is also an award or society of knights granted as recognition.

clue.text: To a chic sort, appear disorganised

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange afresh, so the preceding letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stylish person looks down on a messy-looking crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' reads as a noun for a kind of person, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in total confusion and lacking any order is chaotic, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Chance to reflect disgust expressed by writer

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pah is an exclamation voicing disgust
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author gets the opportunity to voice their revulsion in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chance' is a verb here, as in 'chance to meet'.
explanation.definitionFit: To chance upon something is to happen upon it; both verbs mean occur or come about by accident.

parts.note: taken as written
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Sizing up a horse, as a judge at a show might.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity or total of something is its measure, so the noun is a general synonym.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: so valuable no figure could be put on it
second meaning, read literally: without a price tag

explanation.surface: An heirloom is treasured, yet nobody has ever appraised it.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses seem to contradict each other: one says beyond any price, the other says lacking a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invaluable is precious; split as price-less, the word also means having no price attached.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: critics' write-ups of a play or book

explanation.surface: An actor reads what the critics wrote the morning after.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means spots or heeds; as a plural noun it is the press verdicts on a performance.

clue.text: Blended oats taste poor with cooked vegetables

indicators.note: blended things are mixed together, so the following letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A porridge mix tastes bad served alongside a plate of veg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like a second instruction to rearrange, but its letters are part of what is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast potatoes are a vegetable dish cooked in an oven, the classic side for a Sunday roast in Britain.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dark, lightly hopped British beer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' suggests lemonade; the words split into an adjective and a type of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle weather or temper is described as mild, and mild ale is a traditional low-strength British beer.

clue.text: Goals I stop upset the defenders

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over and disturb, so the preceding letters fall into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper boasts that the saves he makes annoy the back line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defenders' looks like footballers, but it means people who argue in support of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in support of a doctrine or person, so such people are defenders of it.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an orange root vegetable
second meaning: a reward dangled to motivate

explanation.surface: Cheering on a bonus scheme, as if rooting for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root for' reads as the phrase meaning support; here 'Root' is a vegetable and 'for' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange taproot is a familiar vegetable, and from the carrot-and-stick image it also means a tempting reward.

parts.note: surface reading: a detention handed out at school during the term
setter's reading: a court's penalty of a term served in prison

explanation.walkthrough: Term-time sounds like the school calendar, but a term here is a period of imprisonment imposed by a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's ruling fixes a prison term, so the punishment of doing time is literally that judgement.

clue.text: Using moulded steel, manage to take an optical instrument

indicators.note: moulded material is pressed into a new shape, so the metal's letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
to cope is to manage or get by

explanation.surface: A craftsman works shaped steel to build a lens instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tube of lenses or mirrors that makes distant objects look nearer, the classic optical device.

parts.note: an extract is a passage taken from a book
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor has secured a chapter of a book for publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw it out or get it, so the past form means got or acquired.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the room where military personnel eat
second meaning: an untidy or chaotic state

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the canteen is in a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: In the forces the eating hall is called by this name, and the same word means utter disorder.

clue.text: This way is a touch hard

parts.note: a pat is a light touch
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone warns that the route ahead is somewhat difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A track or route to follow is a way, so the noun is a direct synonym for a road taken.

indicators.note: to style something is to fashion it into a new form, so the word's letters are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet shop offers a simpler kind of chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' suggests a fashion or kind, but it signals that the letters of the first word are restyled.
explanation.definitionFit: Praline is a sweet made of nuts cooked in sugar, used as a chocolate filling, so a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Stops inclusion of a fashionable mode of transport

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the next small word goes within the first word

parts.note: to stem a flow is to stop it
taken as written
hip means trendy

explanation.surface: Someone halts the introduction of a trendy way of getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by steam engines carried passengers and cargo, so it is a means of travel.

clue.text: Engages in conversation concerning account expenses

parts.note: AC is a common abbreviation for account
costs are outgoings

explanation.surface: Someone talks to staff about the bills on a business account.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and speak to them, often boldly, which starts a conversation.

clue.text: Nell's is all wrong, so make a complaint

indicators.note: letters that are all wrong are in the incorrect places, so they must be put right by reordering

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Nell has got everything wrong, so someone lodges a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance, but it means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical complaint is a disorder or ailment of the body, so it is a synonym for sickness.

parts.note: surface reading: a member of the armed services
setter's reading: a man whose job is domestic service in a large house

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that service means waiting at table, not military service.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief male servant of a household, who serves wine and meals, is literally a man in service.

indicators.note: something detected in a liquid is found inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: part means some of something
aqua is the Latin for water

explanation.surface: A garden poison has been found in a water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraquat is a powerful, highly toxic herbicide used to clear weeds, so it is a named weedkiller.

clue.text: Coup destroyed the French part of the building

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so its letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
la is French for the, feminine form

explanation.surface: Rebels in a coup wrecked a French building.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small dome on top of a roof, so it forms a part of a building's structure.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lying flat, face down

explanation.surface: Someone tends to tell untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' suggests telling lies; it means lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being liable to something is being prone to it, and the same adjective describes a body stretched out face downward.

clue.text: They produce drinks for detective and ploughman in seconds

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it, so the earlier pieces go within the doubled letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, doubled for the plural
a tiller is one who tills the soil

explanation.surface: A policeman and a farm worker are given a second helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Distillers make spirits such as whisky and gin by distillation, so they are makers of drinks.

clue.text: Sign on both sides of motorway confused one

indicators.note: being on both sides of something means flanking it, so those letters surround the road abbreviation
confused things are muddled up, so the letters of the last word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
M is the prefix for a British motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A motorist is bewildered by signposts on either side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a road sign, but it is a portent.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent of what is to come, so it is a sign in the prophetic sense.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to continue or survive
second meaning: to put up with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Last stand' suggests a final heroic battle, but both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going over time and to tolerate something hardship both translate as this one verb.

indicators.note: changing something alters its form, so the letters are rearranged into a different word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off to get changed before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows' looks like a noun for performances; it is the verb, as in shows someone to a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to guide or escort them to their place, so the verb means shows in.
